## Natural history notes

A small native annual herb in the dayflower family, characterized by narrow, grass-like leaves and delicate pink to rose-purple flowers with three petals. Scrub Roseling occurs primarily in dry, sandy habitats of Florida and Georgia, particularly scrub, scrubby flatwoods, and open high-pine communities. It grows close to the ground in open patches where competition from taller vegetation is limited and is well adapted to the nutrient-poor soils and periodic disturbance characteristic of these ecosystems. The species is also treated under the accepted name Callisia ornata, with Cuthbertia ornata retained as a synonym.
